letter1626.summary: Olivares tells the Duke of Alba of his griefs of summer 1626: the death of a young Guzmán nephew meant for the Church; his daughter María's stillbirth, her recovery, then her death; her virtue. He keeps her widower Ramiro, Marquis of Toral, as son and heir of his house: the dukedom of Medina de las Torres on the commandery of Caravaca, the office of sumiller de corps given by the King of his own motion; he puts his life in the King's service and hopes the Duke his son will behave wisely.
letter1626.en:
‹…› = unresolved word; … = words lost in the gutter (ff. 13v, 14v); [x] = word restored or supplied for the sense. "His Majesty" stands for the code "hol" (probable). The translation follows the reading page by page; where the gutter cuts a line, the sentence is given in fragments.

f. 13r. I have had much to offer to God these days, almost all the causes of grief that I can fear as a father and as master of my house having come upon me together. ‹…› de Guzmán, my nephew, died, a youth of ‹…› years [who] ‹…› in his gifts and in the promise he showed, and the one I had chosen to serve the King and the Church in that dignity. In my grief at this blow, which was in my ‹…› ‹…› the cause and the qualities, God prepared me, not without particular providence, for another, incomparably greater, with which He was to try me.
